<header class="page-hero about-hero">
<p class="eyebrow">Experience & approach</p>
<h1>I work between the biology and the decision.</h1>
<p>My background covers antibody immunotherapies, precision oncology, developmental neurobiology and building computational tools. The job has been the same in all of them: take a question, pull evidence from whatever modalities are available, and say plainly what the data supports and what it does not.</p>
</header>

<section class="about-intro" aria-labelledby="profile-title">
<figure>
<div class="about-photo" role="img" aria-label="Portrait of Rafael Soler Ortuño"></div>
</figure>
<div>
<p class="section-index">Profile</p>
<h2 id="profile-title">Computational biologist with 6+ years across industry and academia.</h2>
<p>I have a PhD in bioinformatics and two years of postdoctoral work in immuno-oncology and tumour biology, using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, multi-omic integration and machine learning for biomarker discovery, validation and patient stratification. In industry that has meant antibody immunotherapies against TNFR2 and FcγRIIB, mode-of-action studies, and translational work in oncology and autoimmune disease.</p>
<p>The useful part is that I know the biology and can also write the code. I can pick up a question at experimental design and QC and carry it through integration, modelling and interpretation to something an experimental or clinical team can use. The pipelines are R and Python, they run on HPC and AWS, and they are meant to be rerun by someone who is not me.</p>
<p>I have worked in Spain, Germany, the United Kingdom and Sweden, and I am comfortable presenting to people whose background is nothing like mine.</p>
<div class="mini-facts">
<span><strong>Current</strong> BioInvent International</span>
<span><strong>Based</strong> Lund, Sweden</span>

<p class="section-index">Career</p>
<h2 id="career-title">Professional experience</h2>

<div class="experience-list">
<article class="experience-entry">
<div class="experience-meta"><span>Aug 2025 – Aug 2026</span><span>Lund, Sweden</span></div>
<div class="experience-content">
<p class="company">BioInvent International AB</p>
<h3>Bioinformatics Research Scientist</h3>
<div class="role-keywords"><span>Single-cell &amp; spatial omics</span><span>Immuno-oncology</span><span>Autoimmune disease</span><span>Antibody drug programmes</span><span>Biomarker discovery</span><span>Target validation</span><span>AWS &amp; HPC</span><span>Agentic AI</span></div>
<ul>
<li>Ran the multi-omic analysis for the BI-1206 anti-FcγRIIB and BI-1808 anti-TNFR2 antibody programmes. The evidence covers scRNA-seq, CITE-seq, spatial transcriptomics, bulk RNA-seq, proteomics and clinical metadata, tied together across patient, mouse and in-vitro samples, and the questions are mode of action and resistance.</li>
<li>Traced an unexpected immune activation mechanism behind an antibody response from clinical single-cell data, and extended the mode-of-action pipeline to handle that kind of patient cohort.</li>
<li>Characterised drug mechanism of action with scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics and targeted gene-module scoring, which resolves antibody-responsive immune cell states, macrophage polarisation profiles and tissue niches in blood and tumour microenvironments. All of that feeds into early patient selection.</li>
<li>Validated cell-type-specific genetic regulation of a candidate autoimmune target using public single-cell data, auditing the raw data quality first so the numbers could be trusted. The result fed a go/no-go decision on the target.</li>
<li>Built biomarker and target evidence for autoimmune and inflammatory disease by curating and integrating public single-cell and spatial atlases across a broad range of conditions: rheumatologic disease, including rheumatoid arthritis with a focus on synovial pathology, systemic lupus erythematosus, juvenile idiopathic arthritis and juvenile dermatomyositis; gastrointestinal and hepatobiliary inflammation, including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis in both human and mouse, and primary sclerosing cholangitis; inflammatory skin disease, including psoriasis and preclinical MC903 and oxazolone mouse models; atherosclerosis; interstitial lung disease; and kidney transplant biology and graft rejection.</li>
<li>Built the biological rationale for a bispecific target by bringing clinical single-cell and spatial transcriptomics into the biomarker strategy. It showed a significant expression correlation with a canonical regulatory T-cell marker before any experimental validation had run.</li>
<li>Built and trained a variational autoencoder to pull strain-level technical variation apart from tumour biomarker signal across genetically diverse mouse strains. It is meant to carry candidate biomarkers over to human population heterogeneity.</li>
<li>Acted as the computational contact point for more than four teams working several projects at once, turning multi-omic results into plain language and helping shape decisions from experimental design through to which validation experiments to run next. Delivered a reusable single-cell and spatial immune atlas and an AWS and Docker HPC environment I built from scratch, both documented so anyone on the team could rerun and build on the work.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</article>

<article class="experience-entry">
<div class="experience-meta"><span>Sep 2020 – Sep 2024</span><span>Alicante, Spain</span></div>
<div class="experience-content">
<p class="company">Institute of Neurosciences, CSIC-UMH</p>
<h3>Bioinformatics Research Scientist · PhD</h3>
<div class="role-keywords"><span>scRNA-seq &amp; ATAC-seq</span><span>Multi-omic integration</span><span>Cross-species genomics</span><span>Deep learning</span><span>Reproducible pipelines</span></div>
<ul>
<li>Built automated Python, R, Bash and AWK pipelines to integrate RNA-seq and ATAC-seq across phylogenetically distant species. That separated the genes and enhancers of cortical development that are conserved from the ones that are not.</li>
<li>Integrated scRNA-seq with RNA-seq and ATAC-seq to define conserved cortical stem-cell types and their gene-regulatory programs across species.</li>
<li>Identified tumour gene signatures in paediatric brain tumours by meta-analysis of public GEO and EGA datasets, then benchmarked them against mouse scRNA-seq, ATAC-seq and bulk RNA-seq models.</li>
<li>Applied deep learning to protein sequence data to predict candidate transcription factors from structural features, and ran the workflow across large public datasets.</li>
<li>Built and published an interactive R Shiny single-cell atlas so researchers who do not code could work with the cortical data themselves. Mentored two MSc students.</li>
</ul>
</div>
</article>
